# Choosing whether pending wakes survive

`message_queue_mode` decides what happens to wakes that arrive while an instance
is busy. `coalesce` keeps only the newest; `backlog` keeps every one. The
template declares a default and each instance may override it.

## The template

```yaml
name: queue-mode-demo
version: "1"
message_queue_mode: coalesce
messages:
  - type: ops/wake
    body_schema:
      type: object
      properties:
        n: {type: integer}
      required: [n]
nodes:
  - type: worker
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: ops/wake
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          n:
            type: integer
            source: "{{messages.ops/wake.n}}"
```

## Two instances, two modes

The first takes the template's default; the second overrides it at create time.

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"template":"'"$TPL"'","instance_key":"coalescing","target_daemon":"my-daemon"}'

curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"template":"'"$TPL"'","instance_key":"backlogged","target_daemon":"my-daemon",
       "message_queue_mode":"backlog"}'

curl -sS "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID"
# message_queue_mode: coalesce | backlog
```

## Back the queue up

Hold the first frame open with a pause-mode `before_dispatch` breakpoint, then
fire four numbered wakes at each instance:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/breakpoints" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"matcher":{"node_type":"worker"},"checkpoint":"before_dispatch","mode":"pause"}'

for n in 1 2 3 4; do
  curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages" \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: wake-$n" \
    -d "{\"type\":\"ops/wake\",\"payload\":{\"n\":$n}}"
done

curl -sS "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages"
```

## What the product does

**While the frame is held.** The coalescing instance has cancelled wakes 2 and
3 and kept 4 pending. The backlog instance has 2, 3 and 4 all pending and none
cancelled.

**After the drain.** Resume every breakpoint hit until the queue empties.

The coalescing instance delivered wakes 1 and 4 across two frames, and never
delivered a cancelled wake. Its node saw payloads 1 and 4. The slow instance
tracked the latest wake instead of falling further behind.

The backlog instance delivered all four across four frames, and its node saw all
four payloads.

## Coalescing drops payloads too

Every wake above carried a body conforming to the declared schema, and two were
dropped. The mode applies uniformly to every message type on the queue. An
operator who needs every payload chooses `backlog`; a payload is not exempt.

## The choice is closed

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"template":"'"$TPL"'","instance_key":"x","target_daemon":"my-daemon",
       "message_queue_mode":"newest-only"}'
# 400 — the error names backlog and coalesce
```
